name: Hamlet
description: Prince of Denmark, son of the late King Hamlet and Queen Gertrude, nephew to the new King Claudius. A student at Wittenberg called home by his father's death, he is charged by his father's ghost with revenge — and spends the play thinking, feigning madness, and delaying.

name: King Claudius
description: The new King of Denmark, who has murdered his brother (Hamlet's father), seized the throne, and married the widowed queen. Outwardly a capable, smooth-talking ruler; inwardly guilt-ridden and increasingly murderous.

relationships.relation: uncle and stepfather of; murdered the father of

name: Queen Gertrude
description: Queen of Denmark, Hamlet's mother, who married Claudius within two months of her first husband's death — the 'o'erhasty marriage' that disgusts her son.

name: Polonius
description: Lord Chamberlain, chief counselor to Claudius, and father of Laertes and Ophelia. A long-winded, self-satisfied schemer whose meddling gets him stabbed through a curtain.

name: Ophelia
description: Daughter of Polonius, sister of Laertes, and the object of Hamlet's courtship. Pressured by the men around her, rejected by Hamlet, and bereaved of her father, she goes mad and drowns.

name: Horatio
description: Hamlet's friend and fellow scholar, level-headed and loyal. He is the witness Hamlet trusts, and the one left alive to 'tell my story.'

name: Laertes
description: Son of Polonius, brother of Ophelia. Hot-blooded where Hamlet is reflective, he returns from France to avenge his father and sister, and is manipulated by Claudius into the fatal duel.

name: Ghost of Hamlet's Father
description: The spirit of the dead King Hamlet, who reveals that he was murdered by Claudius and commands his son to avenge him while sparing Gertrude.

name: Rosencrantz
description: A former schoolfellow of Hamlet, summoned by Claudius to spy on him. Paired almost inseparably with Guildenstern.

name: Guildenstern
description: A former schoolfellow of Hamlet, recruited with Rosencrantz to spy on him, and sent with him to England carrying their own death warrant.

name: Osric
description: An affected, foppish courtier who brings Hamlet the challenge to the duel with Laertes.

name: Marcellus
description: An officer of the watch who, with Bernardo, first sees the Ghost and brings Horatio to witness it. Speaker of 'Something is rotten in the state of Denmark.'

name: Bernardo
description: An officer of the watch who has seen the Ghost on the previous nights and helps persuade Horatio it is real.

name: Francisco
description: A soldier on guard at the play's opening, 'sick at heart,' relieved by Bernardo.

name: Reynaldo
description: Polonius's servant, sent to Paris to spy on Laertes and spread useful rumors about him.

name: Fortinbras
description: Prince of Norway, whose father was killed by Hamlet's father. His decisive pursuit of honor and his army marching across Denmark are a foil to Hamlet's delay; he inherits the Danish throne at the end.

name: Voltimand
description: A Danish courtier sent as ambassador to Norway to check Fortinbras's threatened invasion.

name: Cornelius
description: A Danish courtier sent with Voltimand as ambassador to Norway.

name: First Player
description: The lead actor of the travelling troupe, who delivers the Hecuba speech and plays in 'The Mousetrap.'

name: Player King
description: The king in 'The Mousetrap,' the play-within-the-play staged to catch Claudius's conscience.

name: Player Queen
description: The queen in 'The Mousetrap,' whose protests of eternal fidelity prompt Gertrude's line 'The lady doth protest too much.'

name: First Gravedigger
description: The chief grave-digger ('Clown'), whose grim wit and riddles open Act 5 and who unearths the skull of Yorick.

name: Second Gravedigger
description: The grave-digger's companion, straight man to the First Gravedigger's jokes.

name: Priest
description: The cleric who conducts Ophelia's truncated funeral rites, hinting at the suspicion that she died by suicide.

name: Captain
description: A Norwegian captain in Fortinbras's army who tells Hamlet that thousands will die over a worthless patch of Polish ground.

name: Sailor
description: A sailor who delivers Hamlet's letter to Horatio reporting his escape from the ship to England.

name: Messenger
description: A messenger who brings news to the court, including Laertes's return at the head of a mob.

name: Gentleman
description: A courtier who describes the mad Ophelia before her entrance in Act 4.

name: Lord
description: A courtier who confirms the arrangements for the duel between Hamlet and Laertes.

name: First Ambassador
description: An English ambassador who arrives at the play's end to report that Rosencrantz and Guildenstern have been put to death.

name: Prologue
description: The speaker of the brief rhymed prologue to 'The Mousetrap,' the play-within-the-play.

name: Lucianus
description: The poisoner in 'The Mousetrap,' 'nephew to the king' — a role that pointedly mirrors Hamlet's own threatened revenge on Claudius.

name: Servant
description: A servant who announces the sailors bringing Hamlet's letter to Horatio.
